headline: More than half of finance chiefs at large UK companies expect to cut staff because of AI over the next year, a Deloitte survey finds.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a named survey with clear numbers on jobs and AI, but it measures expectations of 66 executives, not cuts already made.
importance_line: Staff at large UK employers are the people most exposed if the 52% of surveyed finance chiefs act on their expectations, but this is a survey of what executives expect, early in AI adoption, not a count of jobs lost.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Deloitte, the accounting and consulting firm, found in its quarterly survey of chief financial officers at large UK companies that 52% expect to cut headcount because of AI, while 67% say they have achieved only about a quarter of the AI-driven changes they ultimately expect. The survey measures expectations rather than job cuts already made; Reuters, reporting the same Deloitte survey, says it polled 66 finance chiefs between 17 September and 1 October.
notes: Bloomberg text opened only to its paywall (first two paragraphs); the key figures are in those paragraphs. BigGo Finance relayed the Bloomberg report with the same figures; Reuters (via Global Banking & Finance Review) gave the survey sample. Deloitte's own page was not readable.
